transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Since my wife’s fall, I just haven’t been myself. I used to be the one with the lists and a plan for everything. Now I sit at the kitchen table looking at her medication chart and either cry or get irritated over little things. Bills are piling up, I’m not returning my mentoring calls, and even the housework feels like too much. I can’t seem to make myself function.
Did these changes start after your wife’s fall?
Yes. Her fall was about two months ago. I started falling apart once the caregiving routine really took over, not before that.
Since this started, have you felt down or depressed most days?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most days. I’ve been overwhelmed and not myself, but I don’t really know how to separate that out.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?
I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve got a lot on my mind, but I don’t know if it’s what you’d call excessive worrying.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t thought about it in those terms.
Lately, have you been feeling sad or down?
I don’t know. I’ve been feeling pretty overwhelmed, but I can’t really tell if I’d call it sad or down.
Have you stopped enjoying the things you usually like to do?
I’m not sure I’ve stopped enjoying them exactly. I just haven’t really paid much attention to it.
Do you find yourself worrying most of the day?
I’m not sure. I mean, I do feel overwhelmed a lot, but I haven’t really noticed whether I’m worrying most of the day.
Do you feel nervous or on edge much of the time lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to whether I feel on edge most of the time.
When your wife’s care needs are lighter or someone else helps out, do you feel noticeably more like yourself?

I don’t really feel like myself much lately. Since her fall, I’ll sit there staring at the medication chart, and sometimes I just cry, or I snap over something small. The bills and housework keep piling up. I used to have a plan for everything, and now I just can’t seem to make myself do it.
Have you been feeling sad most days lately?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really kept track of whether it’s been most days.
In the past two months, have there been times when you couldn’t enjoy things that usually bring you pleasure?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about whether I’m enjoying things less than usual.
During the past two months, have there been days when you clearly felt sad or down?
I’m not sure. I know I’ve been overwhelmed, but I couldn’t tell you which days I clearly felt sad or down.
When someone else takes over your wife’s care for a while, do you feel noticeably better?

No, not really. Even when someone else is handling things for a bit, I’m still sitting there looking at the medication chart, feeling overwhelmed. I’ll cry or get short-tempered over little things, and I just can’t seem to get myself moving on the bills or the housework.
Lately, have you been having trouble concentrating?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed whether my concentration has been different lately.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether my energy is lower than usual.
Since this started, have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure, to be honest. I haven’t really noticed whether my sleep has changed.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living or that you would be better off dead?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really had a chance to think about it in those terms.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about killing myself specifically.
Since your wife’s fall, has this made it hard for you to keep up with your usual responsibilities?
Yes. I’ve stopped going to my mentoring and community commitments. Even the regular things at home—paying bills, keeping up the house, basic routines—they’re slipping badly.
